Theorem
[The nonhomogeneous transport equation holds along characteristics]

↗ def:transport-nonhom-solution

1. ch2:2.1.2-thm-2\group Transport Equation

If $f$ is continuous, then \[ \left.\frac{d}{dr}\right|_{r=0}u\bigl((x,t)+r(b,1)\bigr)=f(x,t). \] If $u$ is differentiable, this is $u_t+b\cdot Du=f$.
Proof

\sketch Along $(b,1)$ the homogeneous term is constant, while the integral becomes an integral with fixed integrand and upper endpoint $t+r$. The fundamental theorem of calculus gives the displayed derivative.

□
